question: Hold the description and the dog's choices still. Let each swarm build everything else from the bottom up. Do the choices survive, and is each world its own?

swarms.name: Terry Gilliam
swarms.made: The real archive dog from a 1930s home movie, cut out by its mask and engraved by hatching its own light; card parts on pins, a tail cut from its own back fur. Every other figure is a found public-domain cut-out, engraved the same way.
swarms.moved: Card pivots, held frames and hard substitution. The call turns the woman's head into a hinged shouting mouth and the dog's head into a door; the refusal is the card turned over to its blank back, stamped NO; the approach is earned by the door swapped for a lit slab; the lying is a lying card.
swarms.trick: Each choice is a substitution, so the dog's decision is also the film's cut.
swarms.dog: the real archive dog, cut out and engraved, on card pivots

swarms.name: Lotte Reiniger
swarms.made: A hand-cut shepherd silhouette of 23 pieces on 22 pins, its proportions measured from the archive dog's pose keys (not traced). Tissue hills, a card house front, black card with holes the lamp shines through, lace-cut ornament.
swarms.moved: Articulated joints on a lit screen, paws planted by a contact solver; turns are made by swapping in cut end-on pieces (a rear view, a front view) and four interchangeable heads, and the head always leads the body.
swarms.trick: No colour on any figure: the whole relationship has to read by outline and the gap between shapes.
swarms.dog: a hand-cut silhouette of 23 pieces on a lit paper screen

swarms.name: Max Ernst
swarms.dog: an engraved maquette that wears, then absorbs, a found lion's mane
swarms.made: One plate of a collage-novel: a porch at dusk cut in wood-engraving line by one burin, so the seams hide. The person's commanding head is a lion cut from Andy's Animal Alphabet; the hand from The Door to Heaven; a miner's lamp from Anthracite. The dog is a solid maquette of 27 cones and ellipsoids, engraved along its form; no picture of a dog is used.
swarms.moved: The dog turns as a solid in the plate's camera and walks on a step solver. The collage moves by changing job: the lion's head leaves the person and becomes the keystone, whose knock opens the door; the same lion's mane is pasted on the dog with its white cut edge at the first call, and sinks into its coat, edge lost, as it lies across the sill. The grabbing hand returns small and low.
swarms.trick: Authority becomes architecture, then the dog's own fur.

swarms.name: Frank Mouris
swarms.made: Thousands of tiles cut from 55 public-domain archive shots (2,238 frames), each figure a computed shape whose edge is the tiles themselves, down to 4×3 pixels, with no line drawn; the tiles' subjects mean something: the dog is animals and the archive dog, the person faces and hats, the door doors and ladders, the light lanterns and bulbs, the words alarm clocks and trumpets for COME HERE, flowers and swans for it's all right.
swarms.moved: The torrent's speed is the dog's state: frantic under the calls, every tile of the dog replaced at each choice, settling as it lies down, and still holds where each tile only plays its own shot forward.
swarms.trick: The voice is made of pictures too, and it hits the dog as a ring of alarm clocks.
swarms.dog: a torrent of tiles cut from 55 archive shots

swarms.name: Yuri Norstein
swarms.dog: hand-cut replacement pieces on its own glass plane, in fog
swarms.made: About twenty glass planes at measured depths: sky, trees, the room, the door, the house front, floors, posts and weeds; six fog layers keyed from public-domain time-lapse cloud footage; a bowl inside the room cut from the home movie. The dog is a library of hand-cut replacement pieces (five body views, crouch and lying stages, heads per view and ear state, leg segments, paws, tail), each traced once from a maquette, given a scissor edge and painted with the archive dog's coat grain.
swarms.moved: A camera that pans, drops and moves in, so parallax comes from real depth. The fog acts in four states: it thickens between door and dog, is drawn toward the door light, parts along the dog's path and hangs still. Focus is an event: it pulls into the room when the door opens and when the dog is told come in. The dog's pieces are chosen and hinged each frame and laid far to near on its own plane.
swarms.trick: Depth, fog and focus decide what the dog can see, and what we can.

swarms.name: John Whitney
swarms.dog: dot-lines of light on a skeleton, locking 3:2 with the house
swarms.made: Only computed points of light. A 3D skeleton whose proportions are the archive dog's measured rig keys; every part a tube of meridian dot-lines with its own harmonic number, winding into helices and unwinding into straight engraved lines every 8 s. The house, the room, the hearth and the person are point-lines too; the moon is a Lissajous trail of the two oscillators.
swarms.moved: The house pulses at 0.40 Hz and the dog breathes near 0.6 Hz. The calls detune the dog, so its lines go ragged and the moon smears; once the circumstances change the two oscillators couple and lock in a 3:2, and the dog's lines stand straight. The gait is a phase relation driven by distance travelled; the turns are true rotations; the sound is the same oscillator bank, a pure fifth when locked.
swarms.trick: Trust is a fifth: the dog comes when its breath locks to the house.

swarms.name: Peter Foldès
swarms.dog: drawn contour keys whose points correspond, blended pose to pose
swarms.made: Contour keys drawn as coordinates: 16 body keys and 10 head keys, each stroke with a fixed point count so that point i is the same place on the dog in every key. The archive dog was studied for proportion, not traced; the person, the house, the door and the dusk are drawn the same way.
swarms.moved: In-betweens are weighted blends of corresponding points, paced to the score; turns pass through drawn rear and front views where a symmetric key swaps its correspondences. Shapes change as consequences: the caller swells and the reaching arm is drawn long; the refusing dog closes into a curl; the door's outline is carried out onto the boards as its light.
swarms.trick: The door's outline is lifted off the door and laid on the porch as the light.

swarms.name: Ivan Sutherland
swarms.made: Points, lines and arcs on a simulated phosphor vector display. The dog is a 24-point graph under 77 hard constraints (bone lengths, joint sides, floor contact, and the threshold itself), its proportions the archive dog's measured bones; nothing else is borrowed.
swarms.moved: A real iterative solver, warm-started every frame, with its residuals on the console. The prompts are light-pen drags: the reach pulls the hand toward the dog until the console says HAND GOAL UNSATISFIABLE. The dog cannot be dragged at all.
swarms.trick: THE DOG IS NOT SELECTABLE: the brief's 'understand it, not control it', said in Sketchpad's own terms.
swarms.dog: a 24-point graph under 77 constraints, solved every frame

swarms.name: Takeo Igarashi
swarms.dog: six drawn sheets bent by an ARAP solver, features held rigid
swarms.made: Six dog drawings drawn in code: a standing profile, standing and sitting back views, a lying sphinx profile, a profile head with collar and tag, and the back of the head. Each is cut into a triangle mesh, with cuts between the forelegs and at the tail notch, and the eye, nose, tag and buttons weighted forty times stiffer. The moon and trees are Quick, Draw! doodles.
swarms.moved: Only by an as-rigid-as-possible solver: handles, a best rotation per triangle, one energy minimized per frame; a triangle that flips is stiffened and the frame solved again. Feet come from a stepping simulation, planted or in the air, never slid. Turns swap whole drawings, bent across by the solver, the head leading. Against weighted skinning on the same mesh, the solver folds no triangles where skinning folds dozens.
swarms.trick: A drawing that bends without ever folding: the dog keeps its shape by solving for it.

swarms.name: MLS deformation
swarms.dog: one painted pelt, folded into a body by moving least squares
swarms.made: A single flat image of a dog's coat, painted in code and laid out like a pelt: dark saddle, both flanks, four legs, head and tail. No archive frame, no skeleton, no cut pieces, no frame swaps. The swarm wrote the moving-least-squares solver itself, in its affine, similarity and rigid forms, and the end card shows the hide with its handles and the same pose in all three.
swarms.moved: Only 48 point handles and 19 line handles move. Affine MLS lifts the flat hide into a body each frame: the flanks fold down like cloth, the legs reach the boards, the head is a rigid cluster of handles so the face does not shear. Paws stay planted until the body moves too far, then step on alternating diagonals.
swarms.trick: There is no skeleton anywhere: the dog bends as one sheet, the way a hide would if handles pulled it.

swarms.name: Video puppetry
swarms.dog: the archive dog's own pixels, cut into pieces and moved as a puppet
swarms.made: Two frames of the public-domain home-movie dog (Amateur Film New Jersey C), cut out with their masks into a body sheet, a rigid head and neck, a tail and four legs; a three-quarter frame of the same dog is swapped in for the turns, a head turned toward the door is cut from the footage for the look back, and a back-of-head piece is cut from the dog's own dark fur with a drawn mask. The hand reaching for the dog is footage from a public-domain film; the person and porch are cut paper made in code. Nothing on the dog is drawn.
swarms.moved: The body sheet bends by a rigid moving-least-squares warp; the head, tail and legs are stiff pieces pinned at the joints, so lying down and walking are rotations of real pixels rather than tears. The performance is computed from the score, not captured from a live puppeteer, and the end card says so.
swarms.trick: Every pixel of the dog is the real dog; only the way its pieces are held changes.

swarms.name: Localized weights
swarms.kind: Bounded biharmonic weights on a lace mesh
swarms.dog: a red cut-paper lace dog, pierced with holes, bent by bounded weights
swarms.made: One cut-paper profile of a dog drawn in code, pierced with lace holes, legs 10–25 mm apart and the ears side by side, in a cut-away dollhouse view of the doorway at dusk; the person is made the same way. No kit or archive material; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: A triangle mesh (5,565 vertices) with 12 bones, 2 point handles and a 6-vertex torso cage; bounded biharmonic weights solved here (cotangent Laplacian, active-set solve), bounded, summing to one and mostly exactly zero, then linear blend skinning. Lifting one foreleg moves the other 0 mm, against 66 mm with naive weights; the end card shows the heat maps.
swarms.trick: Legs a few millimetres apart on a sheet full of holes move independently because the weights stay local across every gap.

swarms.name: Secondary motion
swarms.dog: a long-coated dog of torn crepe and tissue strips whose coat is its body
swarms.made: Torn crepe and tissue paper strips drawn in code, hung in overlapping rows on hidden paper discs, with no solid outline; a paper puppet person with hair, scarf and coat tails, a doorway curtain and reeds by the porch, in a cutaway house seen from the porch side. No kit or archive material; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: Performed primary paths for the rigid pieces (torso discs, neck, skull, muzzle, two-bone legs), and 264 secondary chains on the dog plus curtain, reeds, hair and scarf: spring-dampers toward a rest shape at four substeps a frame, with gravity, gust wind, the draft when the door opens, and collisions with the floor, the dog and the person.
swarms.trick: The secondary motion carries the story: the coat sleeks and stiffens on the refusal, the ears flick to the soft voice, and the coat spreads and settles as the dog lies down.

swarms.name: Pose2Pose casting
swarms.dog: a bank of 41 whole ink-and-wash drawings, cast to the score by a Viterbi path
swarms.made: An illustration bank drawn for this film: 41 ink-and-wash dog drawings set by hand from a construction kit (profile, three-quarter, front and back heads, legs, tail, a dark saddle, a pale ruff and socks), and 13 drawings of the person; the porch, door, room, light and sky drawn as paths. The archive dog was studied for build and markings; no pixel of it is used.
swarms.moved: Only by choosing one whole drawing per frame: each score frame becomes a pose vector, and a Viterbi path picks drawings by pose distance plus a transition cost, so turns pass through the drawn three-quarter and front views and nothing flickers. Walk and backing drawings sit on a gait chart so planted paws stay pinned. Nothing is tweened or warped.
swarms.trick: The performance is a path through a drawer of drawings: casting, not animating.

swarms.name: Learned layered puppet
swarms.kind: A layered puppet fitted to the archive dog
swarms.dog: an 11-layer puppet fitted to the archive dog, generating poses it never showed
swarms.made: An 11-layer puppet (torso, head, tail, two-part legs) cut from one frame of the public-domain home-movie dog and fitted to its other frames by render-loss optimisation, learning each layer's texture per view and a model of joint angles that scores every generated pose. Hand corrections (lying legs, the look back, the back of the head) are listed on the end card beside the model's own output.
swarms.moved: A gait planner plants the feet and two-joint IK solves the legs; turns are fast cuts through the learned three-quarter views; the head has its own view for the look back.
swarms.trick: The end card shows what the model makes alone next to what had to be corrected by hand.

swarms.name: JibJab
swarms.kind: Cast heads on a cut-out body
swarms.dog: a real archive body wearing a swappable cast head
swarms.made: The body is cut from frames of the public-domain home-movie dog (Amateur Film New Jersey C): torso, neck, forelegs and hind legs from one walking frame, the tail from another, graded warm with the film's own grain kept. The dog's own turn in the footage supplies the turn plates, with its head removed and the gap filled from the coat. Three casts are made for the head slot (a paper head, a Quick, Draw! doodle and a head rebuilt from the home movie), each in five views.
swarms.moved: The body pieces are re-posed on one performance, and a stepping solver plants the feet. Head views are swapped by facing and registered to a socket point on the neck, so the head leads every turn. The end card plays the same performance with each of the three casts.
swarms.trick: The performance belongs to the body; the face is a slot anyone could be cast into.

swarms.name: South Park lineage
swarms.dog: flat construction-paper pieces, a whole drawing per view and posture
swarms.made: Biscuit: about 25 flat construction-paper pieces cut in code, each with a fixed scissor wobble so it looks the same every frame; three body views, five head views, a standing and a lying drawing, and an atlas of eyes, brows and ears. Maren, the person, has one view, stand, crouch and sit postures and a ten-drawing mouth atlas. Five Quick, Draw! doodles make the moon, trees and fence. Original designs, not the show's.
swarms.moved: Every turn or change of posture is a swap to another whole drawing, held on twos, never squashed; the head is turned separately from the body and leads it. Paws are put down and stay put; one list of timed sounds drives her mouth and her voice. The limited animation does the acting: a held sulk, eyes rolled up on the approach, one back-of-head drawing for looking in.
swarms.trick: The fewer drawings it has, the more each choice of drawing says.

swarms.name: Cartoon Saloon lineage
swarms.dog: a painted turnaround sheet, swapped by substitution, rigged only in the legs, tail and neck
swarms.made: Every drawing written as control points for this film: tapered brush-ribbon lines with fixed pressure, flat colour with a synthesized watercolour wash and pooled edge. A cut-away house with a patterned room, a hearth and a carved door frame; a dusk porch with spiral-canopy trees. The dog is a turnaround and expression sheet: profile standing, crouching and lying, three-quarter rear, rear, and five heads. Original designs, not the studio's.
swarms.moved: Views swap by substitution, on twos; a restrained rig moves only the legs (two-bone, paws planted), the tail and the neck. One push-in to the threshold, with line weight held constant through the zoom. The room stays dim until the door opens, and the light falls from the doorway as a wedge onto the boards.
swarms.trick: Discipline is what is not rigged: the drawing does the acting, the rig only carries it.

swarms.name: Moho Smart Bones
swarms.dog: an ochre dog in a variable-width ink line, rigged with bones whose angles re-draw it
swarms.made: One variable-width ink line over flat fills on paper grain, drawn in code by the swarm: an ochre dog with a cream bib, muzzle and socks, a house shown in section, a person drawn the same way. Five head drawings (profile, three-quarter front, front, three-quarter back, back) from one landmark sheet. No kit or archive material is used; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: A Moho-style rig of 25 bones (spine, neck, head, two view-control bones, three-bone IK legs, tail and ears). Six Smart-Bone corrective actions are driven by bone angles: the neck turn bulges the shoulder and shortens the neck, the spine curls, the legs fold round the haunch and elbow, and the chin flattens on the paws. Switch layers pick the head view, and a footfall planner keeps weight-bearing feet planted.
swarms.trick: The turns are not tweened: a view bone switches whole drawings while corrective shapes re-draw the joints it bends.

swarms.name: Toon Boom Harmony
swarms.kind: Production rig: drawing substitution and node graph
swarms.dog: a tan cel mutt swapped whole drawing to drawing from a turnaround library
swarms.made: A library of 106 drawings made in code: 57 dog bodies (stand, crouch, three walk cycles, lowering, lying and front, back and three-quarter views), 9 heads including a back-of-head drawing for looking in, ears, tails, person poses and mouths. Ink, tone and rim-highlight passes over a painted dusk porch and a cutaway lit room, with a palette of 27 named colour styles. No kit or archive material; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: A 26-node graph (exposure sheet, library, palette, pegs, element nodes, a neck curve deformer, a tail chain, composites, cast shadow, grade) evaluated each frame. The acting is an exposure sheet shipped as xsheet.json and .tsv: holds on twos, walks on ones, walk drawings chosen by distance travelled so planted feet do not slide.
swarms.trick: Every turn is a substitution that lands on a whole drawing, never a dissolve; the end card shows the real xsheet rows of the head-lead turn.

swarms.name: Photo-to-Actor
swarms.dog: a public-domain home-movie dog turned into a rigged photographic actor
swarms.made: Six frames of the public-domain home movie Amateur Film New Jersey C with their SAM masks: torso, neck, leg segments and tail cut from them and laid on a body template, and five angle heads (front, three-quarter, profile, lowered, back of head). The person, door leaf and lit hall come from Straight Talk (NTIS, public domain), the sky from Top of the Cloud; the house and light are computed and graded to the same grain.
swarms.moved: Landmarks fitted to each head (the automatic fit was accepted on the front and three-quarter heads and corrected by hand on the profile, lowered and back views, with the failures recorded), expression patches for ears, brow and mouth, whole-body sprite replacement for the turns with hard cuts, and two-bone IK keeping planted paws still.
swarms.trick: A dog that only ever walked to a bowl is retargeted, from a handful of stills, to perform all six choices of the score.

swarms.name: Character Animator
swarms.dog: a layered felt puppet whose behaviours do the acting
swarms.made: A digital felt the swarm made (a synthesized fibre texture, fuzzy cut edges, drop shadows between layers, running stitches), cut into named groups exported like a PSD puppet, with swap sets for the views: side, three-quarter and back bodies; profile, front, back three-quarter and back heads. The person and the place are made the same way; no kit or archive material is used.
swarms.moved: A small runtime with Character Animator's behaviours: triggers, view swaps that cut rather than tween, gaze snapping to named targets, blink and breathe, dangle physics on the ears, tail and ponytail, planted-foot walking, and lip sync of the person from the voice track into the twelve standard mouth shapes. The dog's acting is five layered takes of timed control tracks; the end card says no camera or live performer exists here.
swarms.trick: The puppet is never animated frame by frame: it is performed, and the performance is a file of takes.

swarms.name: Spine runtime
swarms.kind: Skeletal runtime with mixed action clips
swarms.dog: a painted game-art dog played by its own skeletal runtime
swarms.made: Painted game-art parts made in code (tan coat, dark saddle, banded gouache shading, brush strokes, a broken outline) packed into one texture atlas of 46 regions: seven head views, four body views as weighted meshes, ears, and lit and shaded leg segments. The set and the person are painted the same way; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: A Spine-shaped skeleton JSON (28 bones, 20 slots in draw order, four two-bone IK legs) and a library of ten action clips (idle, cringe-back, turn-away, lie, look-back, rise, stalk-walk, lie-across, look-in, settle), mixed by a runtime written here on a body track with a head track layered over it. Turns are attachment swaps and slot reorders through 0, 45, 90 and 135 degree views.
swarms.trick: The head leads because it plays on its own track over the body; the end card draws the real track timeline.

swarms.name: Live2D lineage
swarms.dog: a parametric 2D rig: head keyforms, art meshes on deformers, pendulum physics
swarms.made: A parametric rig written from scratch (no Cubism software here): 17 parameter axes in the Live2D style; a head keyform table of 16 yaw by 5 pitch keys over named landmarks, blended bilinearly; body art meshes with saddle, blaze and belly markings on a chain of rotation deformers; eye, brow and mouth controls; the coat studied by eye from the archive dog. The person is a small rig in the same language; the house is drawn in cross-section.
swarms.moved: The eyes move first, the head two or three frames later, the body last. Both turns pass through a chest-facing view rather than a mirror flip, the head leading; a stepping solver keeps paws fixed until they must step; pendulums drive the tail, ears and tag. The camera zooms about fixed points, with a portrait of the dog while it considers.
swarms.trick: Gaze, head and body are three separate decisions, and the dog makes them in that order.

swarms.name: Rive
swarms.dog: a boned vector puppet driven by a three-layer state machine
swarms.made: An artboard of capsule shapes bound to bones: a two-capsule torso with tuck-up, neck, skull, muzzle, curved-triangle ears, a five-segment tapered tail and four two-bone IK legs, with the coat pattern clipped to the torso. Keyed poses (stand, crouch, lie, rest, look in) and looping clips (breath, wag) are mixed by 1D blend states. The house is drawn in section under an oblique camera. Proportions were studied from a public-domain home movie; no archive pixels are used. Rive itself was not available, so the swarm wrote a small runtime with Rive's primitives.
swarms.moved: Typed inputs (numbers, triggers, a boolean) feed three layered state machines: Facing, Body and Attention. Only Facing may rotate the body, and both turns go through the dog's front. A stepping solver plants each foot until its home moves too far, and the head layer leads the body round at 7.46 s.
swarms.trick: The score is played into the puppet as inputs; the dog's choices come out of its own state machine.

swarms.name: PixiJS archive stage
swarms.kind: GPU scene graph of archive fragments
swarms.dog: a dog of 652 public-domain archive fragments on a 3D skeleton
swarms.made: 966 fragments in one 2048 px texture atlas, cut from public-domain archive shots in the kit (coat from the archive dog's own masks, pale fur from a lion, dark ears from a tiger), Quick, Draw! drawings and own work; atlas.json records each fragment's source, frame, crop and mask.
swarms.moved: PixiJS 7.4.2 in headless Chromium: six depth layers, an alpha mask cut to the door, five render textures per frame (dog body, dog head, person, light, stage), a threshold-and-outline shader that turns fragment clouds into a silhouette, and a grain pass; 31 draw calls a frame. The fragments are posed each frame on a skeleton with planted feet.
swarms.trick: Hundreds of small fragments, texture-batched, are held together into one animal by masks and render-texture passes.

swarms.name: Remotion
swarms.dog: typed capsule components compiled from the score, frame by frame
swarms.made: Real Remotion 4 with React, installed in the folder: the score compiled into a typed manifest, one record per frame, that fails on any missing value; frame-pure React components that draw each frame as SVG from its record alone; a dog of 34 tapered capsules and two ear triangles on a 3-D joint graph, its proportions the medians of the archive dog's rig keys; a matte composition of the same dog for measurement. All sound synthesized as events.
swarms.moved: Position along the porch is exactly the score's x; a stepping solver keeps each paw fixed until a step carries it; capsules seen end-on are discs, so both turns pass through the face. Ten frames rendered twice give identical hashes. The licence tier for Remotion's free use is flagged for the operator to confirm.
swarms.trick: The film is a pure function of its description: render it twice and every frame is the same.

swarms.name: Mask and plate foundry
swarms.dog: a dog composited from public-domain home-movie plates cut by animated masks
swarms.made: Public-domain archive plates from the kit: Amateur Film New Jersey C (the dog, the facade and porch, stabilised and median-stacked into a clean plate), Straight Talk (door, room and standing person), Survival Stresses (the seated person) and Door to Heaven (1941, the arm). One standing dog frame is split by masks into body, legs and head; six of the dog's own turn frames carry the turns.
swarms.moved: A layer compositor written for the film: keyframed bezier masks with feather and expand, parented transforms, corner pins from one locked camera, an inverted camera track, holdout mattes at the door frame and sill, luma keys, roto, and one door-light function lighting floor, sill, dog and person. The score drives the dog's root track; feet lock to the floor by distance travelled.
swarms.trick: Plates from different films are pinned, held out and lit until they share one shot, and the dog performs by animating its masks.

swarms.name: GrabCut
swarms.dog: the archive dog cut by its own graph cut, then re-performed
swarms.made: A graph cut written for this film (Boykov–Kolmogorov max-flow), seeded but not decided by the kit's SAM masks, with scribbles from the rig keys, a 2× supersampled cut, colour and texture models and a clean plate of the shot with the dog removed. Nine frames of the home-movie dog, cut and saved with contour and failure masks; the woman and door cut from Straight Talk, the hand from The Door to Heaven, the wall and boards from the dog's own shot.
swarms.moved: Re-performance of the cuts: the dog's real walk mirrored and run backward for the retreat and chosen by distance for the approach; its own turning frames for the refusal; a lying dog assembled from one frame's cut pieces, with the hidden belly a recorded repair; the back of the head from the one frame the home movie shot from behind.
swarms.trick: The cut is the film: every edge of the dog is an argument about where it ends.

swarms.name: SAM 2 proposals
swarms.dog: the real archive dog assembled only from accepted mask proposals, with nothing invented
swarms.made: Precomputed SAM 2.1 mask proposals from public-domain archive films in the kit: 48 accepted frames of the dog in Amateur Film New Jersey C under one object ID, the door from Straight Talk, a hand from Door to Heaven (1941) and a sitter from Survival Stresses. Recorded correction strokes and evidence refusals: no frame shows the dog lying, so its legs are hidden behind a porch board rather than made up.
swarms.moved: Substitution of real frames placed by their measured centroids on the score: the source dog's own step and turn played forward and backward, a confidence proxy (stability times edge agreement) that rejected frames which leak, and a contact sheet of every source frame with its object ID and confidence on the end card.
swarms.trick: Nothing is drawn: when the archive has no evidence of a pose, the film stages around it instead of inventing it.

swarms.name: Alpha Matting
swarms.dog: the archive dog itself, lifted out of its frames with soft fur edges
swarms.made: Every archive frame of the dog is matted with a fur-class alpha, so the edges are fractional, not cut. The woman and the door come from another public-domain film; the lying dog is cut from one matte and labelled as reconstruction.
swarms.moved: By swapping whole matted frames, and by pivoting pieces of a single matte. Premultiplied compositing keeps the edges from picking up the background.
swarms.trick: The dog's edges hold against sky and siding, because the matte, not the outline, decides what is dog.

swarms.name: Forward kinematics
swarms.kind: Jointed toy moved only by forward kinematics
swarms.dog: a carved and painted wooden toy dog on visible brass pins
swarms.made: Cream-painted carved blocks on brass pins, a red felt saddle cloth with two flaps, black drop ears and a red and cream bead tail, rendered in WebGL; a peg-figure person with a cardigan. Everything is made in code; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: A 31-joint graph for the dog and 25 for the person, every world transform the parent times a pivot offset times local rotations, root first, with no IK anywhere. The head pivot has view anchors for profile, three-quarter and rear, blended by angle. Feet are planted only by hand-keyed hip and knee angles, and the remaining foot slip is measured and stated on the end card.
swarms.trick: The joint graph you see is the one that moves it: change a hip and exactly its children follow, saddle cloth and all.

swarms.name: Inverse kinematics
swarms.dog: the rig itself: tapered capsules on drawn joints, every leg solved every frame
swarms.made: A shepherd-type rig: pelvis and chest, neck, skull and muzzle, ears, a seven-link tail and four three-segment legs, drawn as what it is (tapered capsules with rings at the elbows, stifles and hocks) and lit by dusk and the door light. Proportions come only as numbers from the archive dog's rig keys; no archive pixel appears. The person is built in the same language, and the door is a rigid body with friction.
swarms.moved: Analytic two-bone IK with pole vectors and joint limits on every leg, every frame, checked against a FABRIK solver. A footfall planner locks each planted paw in world space and lifts it only when its home has moved or the leg can no longer hold it. The head aims at world targets: the person, the lit boards, the low hand, the room. The person's reach for the dog straightens toward the target and falls metres short, while the reach to the door edge arrives and pushes it open.
swarms.trick: A command is a target the arm cannot reach; the threshold is a target the dog's own chain lays down across.

swarms.name: As-rigid-as-possible
swarms.kind: Engraved mesh, shape kept by a local–global solve
swarms.dog: an engraving on a triangle mesh, bent by an as-rigid-as-possible solve
swarms.made: The dog, the woman and the place are hatch engravings drawn in code, the hatching running along the limbs. The dog is a Delaunay mesh (profile, rear, front, lying and head-turned-in rest shapes), with proportions taken as numbers from the public-domain archive dog. The swarm wrote the Sorkine–Alexa local–global solve itself, with sparse factorisation; the end card shows the rest meshes and their handles.
swarms.moved: About twenty handles at shoulder, hip, neck, tail, paws and ankles drive the solve, which decides every leg bend, the neck, the belly and the ear folds. View changes are single-frame swaps between rest meshes, hidden as the outgoing drawing narrows. On the same handles, the solve keeps every lying frame free of inverted triangles where a naive warp folds dozens.
swarms.trick: The dog bends where its triangles can keep their shape and nowhere else.

swarms.name: MLS gesture warp
swarms.kind: Risograph print bent by moving least squares
swarms.dog: a two-colour risograph dog whose dot screen stretches where it bends
swarms.made: A two-colour risograph print made in code: an orange coat plate and a blue shade and key-line plate, screened in the dog's own print space, in 13 view prints (profile, three-quarter, rear, lying, look-back, look-in). The porch is screened in screen space at a finer pitch. No kit material; all sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: 37 named control anchors with typed moving-least-squares families per layer (rigid skull and ears, similarity legs, tail and neck, affine coat), inverse-distance falloff, a fold guard, and print swaps at the midpoint of fast swings with no cross-dissolve. The dot-grid strain is measured every frame.
swarms.trick: The warp is honest about itself: wherever the print is bent, its dot screen visibly stretches.

swarms.name: BBW auto-rig
swarms.dog: whole frames of the real archive dog, each auto-rigged and bent as one mesh
swarms.made: Whole frames of the public-domain home movie Amateur Film New Jersey C with their own SAM edges, blur and grain, and one frame of Straight Talk (NTIS) for the person; the porch, light and sound are computed.
swarms.moved: Each irregular silhouette is triangulated inside its mask so the mesh never bridges the leg gaps, given point and bone handles placed automatically from its medial axis, and bent by bounded biharmonic weights solved here (bounded, summing to one, stable across frames); views change only through the archive's own turn frames. Heat maps and tests are on the end card.
swarms.trick: No one paints a weight: the found silhouette rigs itself.

swarms.name: Weighted skinning
swarms.kind: One skin over a skeleton, weighted per vertex
swarms.dog: one closed skinned mesh over 27 bones, coated in the archive dog's own film grain
swarms.made: A single closed triangle mesh (about 7,200 vertices) grown by surface nets over a signed-distance sculpture on a 27-bone rest skeleton, with weights from heat diffusion on the cotangent Laplacian (the Pinocchio method), pruned to four bones per vertex. The coat is some 16,000 small patches of film pixels from the public-domain home-movie dog, kept hard-edged so the archive's grain shows. The person is a second skinned mesh in a wool coat.
swarms.moved: Linear blend skinning and dual-quaternion skinning are both implemented; the film uses dual quaternions. A two-panel inset at the lie-down shows linear blend losing volume at the hock beside the fix, and the end card adds the weight maps and a 160° neck-twist stress test. Feet step on a gait clock with two-bone IK and do not slide.
swarms.trick: The joints keep their girth because of how the skin is blended, and the film shows the version that does not.

swarms.name: Dynamic pose selection
swarms.made: Real people's Quick, Draw! dog doodles, chosen by eye from 4,164 and labelled by pose; the house, door, moon, steps, arm and hand are doodles too, drawn on in their makers' stroke order.
swarms.moved: A decoder picks a whole drawing for every pair of frames, with costs for pose, for changing identity and for swapping off a footfall. A drawing is only scaled, moved or mirrored, never bent.
swarms.trick: The dog that turns its back is the same drawing as the dog that comes.
swarms.dog: whole Quick, Draw! doodles by real people, chosen, never bent

swarms.name: Multiview substitution
swarms.dog: a separate drawing for each view, swapped at its own pivots
swarms.made: Separate drawings made in code for this film: three body views (profile, rear three-quarter, rear), lying versions of the rear two, and four head views, the other side by flipping a near-symmetric dog (dark saddle, pale collar ring, dark tail). The archive dog gave markings and proportions only.
swarms.moved: A turn is a swap to the next view, never a squash or a rotation: the head goes first, the body follows one view at a time, the feet step at each swap, and the torso stays on the score's x through every swap. The door is the only thing that rotates, because a door is flat.
swarms.trick: It solves the turns, the place every earlier swarm failed, by never pretending the dog is a solid.

swarms.name: Tabletop capture
swarms.dog: a paper card dog moved by archive hands on a table, tracked from the pixels and replayed
swarms.made: No camera, table or performer existed, and the film says so: a synthesized overhead tabletop plate of white-card puppets with printed fiducial tabs, moved by public-domain archive hands from The Door to Heaven (1941) matted by their SAM masks. The film itself uses new paper skins cut here: 37 body cards and 11 head cards on a cut-away house at dusk. All sound is synthesized.
swarms.moved: Every piece is tracked from the plate's pixels alone: corner-fiducial calibration, per-card fiducials refined by Lucas–Kanade on the card's own printed texture with hand pixels weighted out, texture identification when a hand hides a marker, and hand mattes from a clean-plate difference plus a learned skin model. The recovered rigid transforms and a 358-event stream drive the film; a corner inset shows the capture with its tracks and mattes.
swarms.trick: The acting exists only as data recovered from fingers moving paper, and the film replays it.

swarms.name: Secondary dynamics
swarms.dog: spheres and capsules, with ears, tail, coat and tag on solved springs
swarms.made: A dog solved and drawn in code from spheres and capsules: six torso spheres, neck and head, muzzle, four legs, two ear flaps, a seven-node tail, a collar with a tag; proportions and coat studied by eye from the archive dog, no archive pixel in the film. The person has a scarf; the door is wood on a hinge; there is a shrub.
swarms.moved: The primary motion follows the score, with planted feet that step. Everything secondary is solved, never keyframed: ears, tail, coat, tag, scarf, shrub and the door are springs and dampers pulled toward the pose, colliding with bodies, floor and lap, and dying away in the holds. The person's one push is sized so the door reaches its stop at 6.20 s.
swarms.trick: Nothing secondary is animated by hand, so stillness has to be earned: the holds are quiet because the energy has gone.

swarms.name: Neural layered puppet
swarms.kind: Parts and joints discovered from a few frames
swarms.dog: the archive dog's pixels in eight layers discovered by fitting, with seams and pins left visible
swarms.made: Seven frames of the public-domain home-movie dog, fitted by gradient descent and EM until eight layers and five joints emerged (head, neck, shoulder, fore leg, trunk, back, rump, hind legs). The learned split ties a hand-cut rig on unseen frames; the learned turn poses beat hand-set ones on 13 of 16 archive turning frames, shown side by side on the end card.
swarms.moved: Hand-set rotations on the learned hinges carry the acting; the turns are the puppet posed at its own learned fits of the archive turning frames.
swarms.trick: Nobody drew where the dog's joints are: the fit found them, and the seams stay on screen.

swarms.name: Collage Graph Rewriting
swarms.dog: a graph of typed fragments of one archive dog, rewritten by rule
swarms.made: Head, torso, legs and tail are cut from the archive dog's frames. Other found images make the world: a bulb for the lit room, a cloud for the dusk, a door from a film, and a face from another.
swarms.moved: Thirteen written rules replace, merge, split, enter and exit fragments. The turns are found frames, not mirrored, and the dog is re-cut from sunlit frames as it crosses the threshold.
swarms.trick: Each change to the dog is a named rule, so the film can say what it did and why.

swarms.name: Multiplane parallax
swarms.kind: Spatial collage in depth, with a moving camera
swarms.dog: thirty cut pieces of the archive dog, each at its own depth
swarms.made: Fourteen collage planes at measured depths, from dusk clouds 140 m away (Top Of The Cloud) through trees, a real room behind the door (back wall, lamp, a hinged door leaf from Straight Talk), the clapboard wall at 0 m, the porch and a near railing. The dog is thirty cut-paper pieces textured from the home-movie dog, each set at its own depth so it has parallax of its own; the moon is a Quick, Draw! drawing, CC BY 4.0, credited.
swarms.moved: The camera never rotates: it cranes down, trucks with the approach, and pushes through the railing to the doorway as the dog looks in, so depth is carried by how fast each plane moves. A foot planner keeps planted feet still; the pieces re-stack as the dog turns.
swarms.trick: The room behind the door is a real deeper plane, so looking in has somewhere to go.

swarms.name: Occlusion compositing
swarms.dog: archive cels split by depth, so the door frame decides what is inside
swarms.made: Every element an RGBA layer with a depth, ordered each frame by which layers overlap and which is nearer, and drawn back to front. The dog is the real dog of Amateur Film New Jersey C: its own frames cut by their mattes, its own turn played for the refusal, a lying pose built from cut parts. The hallway and door from Straight Talk, the hand from The Door to Heaven, the bulb and sky found; the house, porch, post and the person drawn.
swarms.moved: The thesis is the ending: the dog lies at an angle into the doorway, its depth crossing the plane of the door frame under the post, so it is split into two layers, the front half behind the post in the doorway and the hindquarters in front on the porch. The door holds back the room's light until it opens; the porch post passes in front of the walking dog; the layer order never loops or flips in any frame.
swarms.trick: Half in, half out is a fact about layers: the door frame is in front of one half of the dog and behind the other.

swarms.name: Face Landmark Registration
swarms.dog: a drawn dog built from view plates, each carrying its own landmark points
swarms.made: Four head plates and three body plates, each with landmarks, fitted onto a 3D skeleton. The person's face is a public-domain cartoon profile placed by a similarity fit, with the mouth driven by the voice.
swarms.moved: Plates are swapped by view as the head turns, so the head leads every turn. The eye and mouth are controls inside the head plate.
swarms.trick: The dog turns through depth by swapping views, never by mirroring a side.

swarms.name: Sound-to-action
swarms.dog: 172 inked drawings, each answer cued by a vowel in the voice
swarms.made: The seven spoken lines synthesized with CMU Flite, whose own phoneme timing is the film's clock; ten profile mouth shapes for the person; a dog of 172 distinct inked drawings in side, three-quarter and rear views; arcs at the mouth and at the dog's ear and paw ticks computed from the audio; every other sound synthesized and panned by screen position.
swarms.moved: A typed list of sound events places each line so that the vowel the dog answers, plus a hearing latency, lands on the score's choice; an exposure sheet names every frame's drawing, mouth, door and light. Drawings change on twos and the body moves only when a new drawing is shown, so planted feet stay planted; the turns pass through drawn views head first.
swarms.trick: The dog answers sounds, not lines: each choice is a measured lag after a vowel.

swarms.name: State machines
swarms.kind: A dog whose refusal is its own decision
swarms.dog: a segmented body posed by its own decision machine, cast into flip-discs
swarms.made: The whole scene is a display board of 320×180 flip-discs and LEDs: what gives light is lit (the sky, the room), what receives light is flipped (dog, person, house). The dog is 27 rounded segments, posed each frame by the machine's body layer and cast into the discs with dark outlines, eye discs and a head line. The spoken words type out on a strip of the board; state names never appear.
swarms.moved: A hierarchical utility state machine ticking 24 times a second, with drives (pressure, fear, memory of being pressed, curiosity, trust) and senses (it hears all round, but sees only where its head points, so with its back turned it misses the door and the low hand). Eleven parameters were tuned until its own choices fell on the score's times; the score's states are never an input. A relay clacks at each decision; the end card shows the states it took and the drive curves.
swarms.trick: Nobody keyed the refusal: the dog decides it, and the board clacks when it does.

swarms.name: Open-content atelier
swarms.kind: Museum open-access objects, cut and recomposed
swarms.dog: one pointer cut from a Currier & Ives print, hinged into every pose
swarms.made: Every actor is a Smithsonian American Art Museum object marked CC0 on both the record and the image: the dog is the pointer from Currier & Ives, Woodcock Shooting (1973.122.4), cut into head, neck, torso, tail and two-part legs; the person is an Edouart cut-paper silhouette (1981.172.33) with an arm from another (1981.172.31); the door is José Dolores López's Screen Door (1989.30.3); the room is from E. F. Andrews's Interior of a House (1916.6.39); the dusk is MacGilvary's Twilight after the Rain (1913.3.3). The Getty hosts were refused by the proxy, so no Getty object is used, and the end card says so.
swarms.moved: The same pieces of the one print are hinged differently for every pose: the creeping stalk of the original print for the approach, the head mirrored about the neck to look back over the shoulder, a fifteen-frame lowering into the lie, and the engraved head reaching level past the jamb into the lit room.
swarms.trick: No line is drawn: every figure is a museum object, recomposed as an actor, with its object number on the card.

swarms.name: Historical print stage
swarms.dog: engraved after the archive dog's own frames, documented and invented kept apart
swarms.made: One plate, Pl. I, The Threshold: a sectional elevation of a wall, doorway and porch at dusk, line-engraved and hand-coloured. The dog is traced by hand from one frame of Amateur Film New Jersey C into eleven pieces, each engraved with a line screen from the scan's own tone; both turns are the film's own frames, some printed as reversed impressions. The door from Straight Talk, the hand from The Door to Heaven. No Library of Congress item is used or claimed.
swarms.moved: Pieces rotate about hand-placed joints, legs by two-bone IK with stance feet pinned. Under the image a key shows the scan frame in use, its source and rights, and the state of the drawing: as photographed, printed reversed, or, in red with red pins at the joints, re-posed as invented motion.
swarms.trick: Every frame says whether the dog in it was photographed or invented.

swarms.name: Mouris montage research
swarms.kind: Montage on a measured cutting score
swarms.dog: one steady dog whose coat, eyes and paws are substituted image by image on a cutting rhythm
swarms.made: 44 crops from 39 public-domain kit frames, tagged by imagery class (fur, hard, eyes, paws, doors, lamps, hands, voices, soft) and temperature, cut flat with a paper margin and a scissor line into the dog's body, neck, head, legs and tail and into the person; cut-letter words. The Mouris collection itself was not viewed or used, and the cards say so; an invisible sphere pose guides the outline, as the end card states.
swarms.moved: A cutting score of whole-image substitutions over the scene: two-frame holds of hard, cold images on the calls, long warm holds on the soft voice, one cut per footfall on the approach; the narrated words appear as letters cut from class-matched images at their spoken frames.
swarms.trick: The rhythm of the cuts carries the drama while the dog stays one animal.

swarms.name: Gilliam Ephemera
swarms.dog: one public-domain home-movie dog, cut into seven pinned pieces
swarms.made: The archive dog is cut into head, torso, tail, two forelegs and two hind legs, pinned at the joints. Substitute cards of the same dog make the turns. A found face in a hat with a hinged jaw, a smock, a bulb, trees and a cloud make the world.
swarms.moved: Pins, slides and swivels; whole-frame swaps for the turns, and a giant hand from above in the moon gag.
swarms.trick: The collage's logic is the dog's own: each piece moves on a pin, and the absurd beat is a hand from nowhere.

swarms.name: Atlanta Moving Image
swarms.made: No drawing at all. The archive dog's own footage, masked frame by frame; the woman and the door from Straight Talk, the seated man from Survival Stresses, the hand from The Door to Heaven, the wall and path from the home movie. A live strip above the stage shows every source frame in use, with its title, year, rights and the operation applied.
swarms.moved: Re-timing and re-ordering recorded motion: its walk mirrored and played backward is the retreat; its own turn away from a person is the refusal; the door's closing swing run backward is the opening. The one pose the footage never recorded, lying down, is composed and marked COMPOSED on screen.
swarms.trick: The scene says what it is the whole time: COMPOSED SCENE · archive fragments re-performed · not a recorded event.
swarms.dog: the archive dog's own footage, re-timed and re-ordered

swarms.name: Provenance graph
swarms.dog: cuts from one archive frame and its own turning frames, every layer hashed
swarms.made: One frame of the home-movie dog cut along its SAM mask and recorded cut lines into head, body and legs, the tail from another frame, each in a dusk and a lamplight colouring; the dog's own turning frames for both turns. The Straight Talk door, a woman cut from Straight Talk, the hand from The Door to Heaven, a miner's lantern from Anthracite, wall stone from the home movie, Quick, Draw! moon, trees and fence. Every image is a node in a 367-node lineage graph with a content hash, its parents, its operation and its rights.
swarms.moved: Pivots and a planted-foot walk for the puppet; hard substitution through single clean archive frames for the turns; the door's closing swing played as its opening. Every frame is composed only from its recorded layers: 287 derived images re-run from source reproduce their hashes, and frames rebuilt from the records alone match the render bit for bit.
swarms.trick: The film can answer, for any pixel, where it came from and what was done to it.
